details: Hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the US-Iran conflict have emerged following statements from US President Donald Trump indicating a desire to hold off on new military strikes and progress in diplomatic efforts. This development has significantly driven down Brent crude prices, with some reports showing them falling to their lowest since August. The easing of geopolitical tensions in the Middle East is seen as reducing inflationary pressures globally and has positively impacted broader stock markets.
title: US-Iran De-escalation Hopes Drive Oil Prices Down

details: A senior South Korean diplomat issued a warning that cryptocurrency thefts, particularly those facilitated by AI-driven cyberattacks, are escalating into significant international security threats. This concern comes after North Korea was accused of stealing over $6 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance. The diplomat urged a comprehensive overhaul of cybersecurity paradigms to address these evolving threats.
title: South Korea Warns Crypto Thefts Pose Global Security Risks in AI Era

details: Nvidia's stock has faced pressure due to an ongoing independent investigation into allegations that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation involving a suspected Chinese spy. This development has sparked broader concerns within the AI sector and highlights the sensitivities surrounding US export restrictions on advanced chip technology to China.
title: Nvidia CEO Under Investigation Amid Chinese Spy Allegations

details: Financial markets are eagerly awaiting the release of the US Consumer Price Index (CPI) report for October, due today, and producer-price data on November 13. These economic indicators are critical for evaluating current inflationary pressures and will heavily influence the Federal Reserve's decisions regarding interest rates at its upcoming December meeting. Analysts are closely watching for any signs of moderation or persistence in price increases.
title: US Inflation Data to Influence Federal Reserve Rate Decision

details: Days before Israel's election, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu suggested utilizing cryptocurrency as a means to circumvent international sanctions. However, this proposal was met with strong opposition from Israeli economists, who dismissed it as "outrageous nonsense," and the Bank of Israel, which explicitly stated that cryptocurrencies cannot be effectively used to bypass sanctions.
title: Netanyahu Proposes Crypto to Bypass Sanctions, Faces Central Bank Opposition
